source.publisher: U.S. National Park Service, Land Resources Division
source.title: NPS unit boundaries

note: National parks and water-related NPS units only; other federal land is not shown.

parks.name: Arches National Park
parks.why: Sandstone arches above the Colorado River near Moab.

parks.name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
parks.why: Sheer gorge on the Gunnison River, a Colorado tributary.

parks.name: Canyonlands National Park
parks.why: Where the Green River joins the Colorado.

parks.name: Death Valley National Park
parks.why: The lowest, driest place in North America; a closed basin.

parks.name: Glen Canyon National Recreation Area
parks.why: Surrounds Lake Powell, the reservoir behind Glen Canyon Dam.

parks.name: Grand Canyon National Park
parks.why: The Colorado River’s mile-deep canyon between Lake Powell and Lake Mead.

parks.name: Lake Mead National Recreation Area
parks.why: Surrounds Lake Mead and Lake Mohave, behind Hoover and Davis dams.

parks.name: Rocky Mountain National Park
parks.why: Where the Colorado River begins, on the west side of the Continental Divide.

parks.name: Yosemite National Park
parks.why: Holds Hetch Hetchy Reservoir, San Francisco’s main water supply, on the Tuolumne River.

parks.name: Zion National Park
parks.why: Canyon cut by the Virgin River, upstream of St. George.
